inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report, consolidated statement of cash flows, 'Share-based payments' add-back 11,584k (TNE.AX_Annual_FY2025.txt:5169); no separate cash tax on net-share settlement is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0), so the add-back is the full figure
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T05:10:28Z regular ASX close (Friday); FY2026 full-year result is due mid-November 2026 and will move this
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average fully diluted shares used for H1 FY2026 diluted EPS, 329,335,105 (TNE.AX_HalfYear_H1-FY2026.txt:73); FY2025 full-year diluted was 329,863,511. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. The FY2025 on-market buyback (A$30.4m) funded the flat count; none in H1 FY2026.
inputs.net_cash_basis: Cash 40.328m + financial assets (term deposits) 205.132m = 245.46m at 31 March 2026 (H1 FY2026 balance sheet, lines 466-467); zero bank debt. Lease liabilities of 49.4m are EXCLUDED from net debt because the lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (treatment B). H1 cash is seasonally low (annual-in-advance billing is H2-weighted; FY2025 year-end was 319.6m) -- the latest filing is used regardless.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated flows discounted at an AUD cost of equity: ACGB 10-year ~4.4% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 = ~9.4%, rounded to 9.5%. No debt, so WACC = cost of equity. Same rate in all three scenarios -- growth, margin and retention risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. FY2025 lease principal repayments 7,150k (financing, line 5360) + interest on lease liabilities 3,496k (line 6583) = 10.65m = 1.78% of revenue, charged via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (49.4m at Mar-26) excluded from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use amortisation (FY2025 total D&A 80,797k less ROU amortisation 6,331k = 74.5m = 12.4% of revenue, note at line 6131) so the lease is not charged twice through the tax line.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- wholly owned subsidiaries, no non-controlling interests.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC, pre-lease (IFRS 16), and excludes interest income: FY2025 PBT 181.5 - interest income 9.7 + lease/other interest paid 3.5 + D&A 80.8 + SBC 11.6 = 267.7m = 44.7% of 598.5m revenue. The company's own Adjusted EBITDA (255.7m, after SBC) ties to this within 0.2m. Capitalised development (~54% of R&D) is NOT in this margin -- it is charged in full through capex_pct_path.
inputs.working_capital_basis: Deferred revenue is 49% of revenue (294.5m at Sep-25) because 91% of revenue is annual-in-advance SaaS. Observed capture of the YoY revenue increase: FY2023 50%, FY2024 41%, FY2025 52%, before receivables growth. Base uses 35% (net of receivables/contract-asset build), bull 40%, bear 25%. This is above the 15-20% house default and is evidenced by the balance sheet, not assumed.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 1: operating SaaS company), 10-year explicit horizon because the component-built owner-FCF margin is still ramping at year 5. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). FY0 is FY2025 (year ended 30 Sep 2025); year 1 is FY2026, substantially complete but not yet reported (results due mid-Nov 2026). Owner FCF 166.8m = reported FCF (OCF 294.5 - capex 106.4 = 188.1m) - SBC 11.6m - interest income 9.7m; after the 10.6m lease cash cost that the projection charges separately, the comparable FY2025 base is ~156m (26% of revenue). Interest income is stripped because net cash (245m) exceeds 1x the FCF base; the cash pile is added back once in the bridge. Buybacks: a repurchaser (A$30.4m FY2025 on-market, neutralising LTI dilution), so the flat count is funded rather than a convention. The market-implied EV/owner-FCF is ~63x and P/E ~78x; the house DCF at a 9.5% AUD discount rate values the explicit SaaS fade materially below the price -- see required_return_table for the return the current price implies.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (ARR +16-18%, PBT +18-20%) tempered by H1 FY2026 revenue growth of 11.5% as SaaS+ shifts consulting into recurring fees; equity CAGR rejected as a growth proxy (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (23.5% 3yr / 26.0% 5yr) exceeds revenue CAGR (17.6% / 14.9%) by more than 30%: book equity was depressed in FY2019 by the AASB 15 transition adjustment and has since been inflated by retained earnings and reserves ahead of the FY2025 special dividend and buyback. It is not a usable growth anchor for this business.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income: FY2020 55.0, FY2021 58.6, FY2022 71.7, FY2023 94.2, FY2024 104.8, FY2025 166.8). Owner-FCF CAGR runs 1.5-3pp below reported-FCF CAGR because SBC (3.3m -> 11.6m) and interest income (0.4m -> 9.7m) both grew faster than cash flow. FY2025 owner FCF was flattered by a 48m deferred-revenue inflow and 64m total working-capital inflow; the component build does not carry that margin forward.

base.growth_note: FY2026 at 14% (ARR guided +16-18%, H1 revenue +11.5%; revenue lags ARR as consulting shrinks under SaaS+). Fades 1pp/yr to FY2030 then faster; FY2030 revenue ~1.05bn implies ARR ~960m, slightly short of management's $1bn+ FY30 target.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC, pre-lease EBITDA 44.7% FY2025 -> 46.0% FY2026 (consistent with PBT +18-20% guidance after ~8-9m Showcase/AI launch costs) -> 49% mature, i.e. ~+4pp operating leverage against management's 35%+ PBT margin target from 30%.
base.capex_note: Capex (capitalised development + contract acquisition costs + PPE) was 17.8% of revenue FY2025 and 18.5% in H1 FY2026 (R&D +22%, ~54% capitalised). Held at 18% in FY2026 and faded 0.5pp/yr to 14% as R&D settles at the low end of the 20-25% range on a larger base. D&A ex-ROU rises toward capex as the capitalised base amortises.
base.tax_note: FY2025 book ETR 24.2% (current tax 25.7%), cash paid 22.7%, versus 30% statutory offset by the R&D tax incentive. Ramped to 27% as the incentive shrinks relative to profit.

bull.growth_note: Top of FY2026 guidance and ARR compounding at 16% through FY2027, hitting the $1bn+ ARR target during FY2029; UK scales to ~15% of ARR.

bear.growth_note: FY2026 revenue growth stays near the H1 run-rate (11%) and NRR settles at ~110%; APAC whitespace saturates faster than management expects and the UK stalls against Civica/Capita incumbency.

scenario_narratives.base: TechnologyOne lands at the top of FY2026 guidance (PBT +18-20%, ARR +16-18%) but revenue grows ~14% as SaaS+ converts consulting into recurring fees, and ARR compounds at a fading 13-10% through FY2030 to land just under the $1bn+ target. NRR holds in the 113-116% band: the installed base of ~1,250 government, council, university and health customers keeps buying modules (ARR per customer >A$490k and rising) while churn stays ~1%. The UK grows 20-25% a year and reaches ~12% of ARR. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands ~4pp to 49% as Showcase/AI launch spend normalises and SaaS+ implementation costs scale, delivering a PBT margin in the low-to-mid 30s against the 35%+ target. Capitalised R&D stays heavy (18% of revenue in FY2026) and fades to 14%; the deferred-revenue working-capital tailwind shrinks with growth. The result is an owner-FCF stream that roughly triples over ten years, which at a 9.5% AUD discount rate and a 3% terminal growth rate is still worth far less than the market pays -- the price embeds a much longer growth runway than a ten-year fade.
scenario_narratives.bull: SaaS+ and the agentic-AI 'Plus' product (launched Feb 2026) lift ARR per deal ~40% and add a transaction-based ARR layer, so ARR compounds at 16% for two more years and passes $1bn during FY2029, a year ahead of target. UK council amalgamation and higher-education wins (Islington, Greenwich, Hertfordshire, Royal Holloway) take the UK to ~15% of ARR, and the 'ERP in 30 days' programme cuts implementation cost enough for the pre-SBC EBITDA margin to reach 52% and PBT margin to exceed 35%. Deferred-revenue capture stays near the 40%+ observed in FY2023-25. Even here, the value only approaches the price if the exit multiple stays well above the 20x owner-FCF cap -- the bull case is a growth story that the market is already paying for.
scenario_narratives.bear: Growth decelerates off the larger base: revenue growth stays at the ~11% H1 FY2026 run-rate as consulting shrinks faster than SaaS fees grow, NRR drifts from 114% toward 110% as APAC whitespace (currently <15% penetration claimed) proves harder to monetise, and the UK stalls against entrenched Civica/Capita incumbency and council budget pressure. Plus/AI features are bundled rather than sold, so the Showcase/AI cost base is not recovered and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin stays ~45-46% while capitalised R&D remains 15%+ of revenue. The A$245m cash pile and ~1% churn mean there is no solvency question -- the bear case is a de-rating from a premium multiple to a mature-software multiple, which is what the November 2025 17% single-day fall previewed.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 20% because NRR has drifted below the 115-120% target (117% -> 115% -> 114%) and H1 FY2026 revenue growth of 11.5% sat well under the 17% ARR print, so the deceleration axis is live rather than hypothetical. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs three independent things -- UK scale-up, AI/Plus monetisation as incremental ARR, and margin expansion to 35%+ PBT -- to land together; management's record of hitting the top of guidance ($500m ARR 18 months early) keeps it from going lower. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value TechnologyOne as the owner of a very sticky, 91%-recurring public-sector ERP franchise: expense SBC fully, strip interest on the cash pile (added back once), charge lease cash cost inside the flows, charge capitalised development in full through capex, and model the deferred-revenue working-capital inflow as a function of growth rather than a permanent margin. Discount in AUD at the cost of equity (no debt). The house answer is what the cash flows are worth to an owner demanding a 9.5% return; the required-return table shows the return the current price actually implies, which is the more useful number for a stock that has always traded on a premium multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: ARR/NRR deceleration: the equity trades on ARR momentum and fell 17% in one day on a 2pt miss; the bear case is a multiple de-rating, not a solvency event

Capitalised R&D (~54% of a 25%-of-revenue R&D budget) flatters reported margins; the model charges it through capex, so a shift to expensing changes optics not value, but a policy change could jolt the share price
Deferred-revenue tailwind: 48m of FY2025's 188m reported FCF was deferred-revenue growth; it shrinks mechanically as growth slows
Terminal value dominates (Gordon at 9.5%/3% implies ~16x year-10 owner FCF vs the ~63x the market pays today); value is very sensitive to the discount rate
FY2026 full-year result (mid-November 2026) and FY2027 guidance will reset the year-1 and year-2 drivers; the price is also exposed to the AUD rate cycle as a long-duration growth stock
UK execution and GBP/AUD translation as the UK grows toward 15% of ARR
